Return the next passage of fiction.

I offer to carry the empty plates back to the kitchen, without offering to take over anybody's work.
</user>

item.text:
“I can carry the empty plates through,” you offer.

Jo glances over the table. “Yes, thanks. Just the plates. Leave the serving dishes where they are.”

You stack the empties and carry them behind the cafe counter. The kitchen is narrow and brightly lit, with new steel worktops squeezed around older tiled walls. Ingredient tubs bear Jo’s block-lettered labels. A separate cluster of tools—knives, scales, a hand mixer—has strips of red tape around the handles.

“Left of the sink,” she says. “The right side is clean.”

You set the stack down without disturbing Owen’s drying rack. He shifts aside to give you space.

“Cheers,” he says.

Jo brings in the remaining plates herself. “That’s useful, thank you. Owen and I can finish from here.”

Nell appears at the hatch with her mug, then looks from the kitchen to the stairs.

“I didn’t explain food arrangements upstairs.”

“We hadn’t settled them,” Jo says. “His room doesn’t have a kitchen, and this one isn’t communal by accident.”

“No. We should make an actual arrangement.”

Jo dries her hands. “I can clear a labelled shelf in the fridge. Kettle and microwave are fine outside cafe service, provided my stock stays separate. We’ll write down the hours once I know the opening routine.”

Nell nods. “That works. I should’ve dealt with it before Rowan arrived.”

“It can be dealt with now.” Jo turns to you. “Have you brought anything that needs refrigerating tonight?”
